text:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: streaming-service p99 latency breached 2.5s across eu-west-1 and us-west-2. SLO violation detected. auto-created incident #INC-4721

tim (oncall): acked. I'm on it, starting triage.

maria (sre): seeing p95 ~800ms, p99 ~2.7s. stream stalls correlate with cache_miss_rate spiking from 4% -> 36% at 04:12 UTC.

eva (eng): noticed a prefix-hash rollout at 04:00 via canary-to-prod job. Deploy ID: deploy-2024-09-21-73f. Did a config tweak to prefix hashing to attempt better distribution.

alex (eng-releases): deploy-bot shows rollout completed at 04:05 to 60% of traffic, then 04:09 to 100%. We have the full diff: changed prefix salt + moved to v2 hashing.

tim (oncall): ok seems suspicious. maria, can you post the cache hit metrics and any KV backend errors?

maria (sre): paste: ```
# metrics snapshot (eu-west-1)
cache_hit_rate: 92% @ 03:55
cache_hit_rate: 64% @ 04:06
cache_hit_rate: 58% @ 04:10
cache_miss_rate: 36% @ 04:12
prefetch_failures: +1200
paging_latency_p99: 210ms -> 1.8s
streaming-tail-queue: backlog +480
```

maria (sre): no widespread KV errors, reads fine; it's a key mismatch pattern. We're getting many prefix-miss keys (new hash keys) and downstream cold-cache thundering.

eva (eng): that matches the code change — v2 hash is not backward-compatible with existing salted prefixes. We expected a migration, but it looks like we shipped 100% without warmup. My bad.

tim (oncall): action plan: 1) Roll back the prefix-hash change to restore hit-rate. 2) If rollback delayed, enable aggressive prefetch/warmup for top 50 prefixes as quick mitigation. 3) Notify top affected customers. Who can execute rollback?

alex (eng-releases): I can coordinate rollback. rollback-preflight indicates safe revert available. ETA ~7m to start controlled rollback (canary then full).

ryan (pm): Heads up — two customers on eu-west noticed errors/latency in cloud-monitoring (support pinged). We should draft a short customer note if we expect >30min impact.

maria (sre): started a live query to surface top missing prefixes: ```
SELECT prefix, count(*) as miss_count
FROM cache_accesses
WHERE hit = false AND ts > '2024-09-21T04:00:00Z'
GROUP BY prefix
ORDER BY miss_count DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

maria (sre): top prefixes look like old-namespace keys; new hash mapping produced different keyspace. Misses concentrated in 5 namespaces (search, chat, rerank, embeddings-lite, streaming-kv).

tim (oncall): eva, can you confirm any migration tool exists? If not, rollback immediately.

eva (eng): no automatic migration. We had a warmup plan that never ran — release notes were wrong. Rolling back now is the correct path.

deploy-bot: rollback job queued: rollback-deploy-73f -> target stable: deploy-2024-09-19-21a. Approval required: @alex.

alex (eng-releases): approved, kicking rollback. Starting canary revert to 5% traffic. Monitoring p99 and cache hit rate.

maria (sre): canary metrics (04:23): cache_hit_rate in canary hosts recovered from 58% -> 89% within 90s. Overall cluster still slow because 95% of traffic still on new keys.

tim (oncall): good sign. Continue rollback to 50% then 100% if stable. Also increase streaming timeouts / graceful retry on the edge to reduce user-visible errors until the rollback completes.

eva (eng): applying edge retry patch now (hotfix): set streaming tail backoff to 100ms, add 2 retries. Pushing config via feature-gate to prod.

maria (sre): alert: prefetch-workers CPU spiked during the warmup attempt; we throttled prefetch to avoid overloading origin. We'll keep prefetch limited to top 50 prefixes only.

tim (oncall): customer comms: ryan draft something short: incident summary, affected regions, mitigation steps, ETA for resolution. Keep it minimal.

ryan (pm): draft: "We saw increased latency in streaming features due to an incompatible prefix-hash rollout. We are rolling back the change and expect service latency to normalize within ~15-30 minutes. Engineers are monitoring and will follow up with a postmortem." Thoughts?

maria (sre): add note about SLO breach and whether customers saw errors: "Some customers experienced elevated latencies and transient errors; no data loss observed."

alex (eng-releases): rollback to 100% at 04:34 completed. Monitoring: p99 dropped from 2.7s -> 420ms within 3 minutes. cache_hit_rate climbed back to 91% cluster-wide by 04:38.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigation complete. SLOs returning to normal. Please confirm customer notifications and schedule a postmortem.

tim (oncall): marking incident as mitigated. I'll hand off to daytime oncall and schedule postmortem with eng/release/sre. Handing to maria for writeup.

maria (sre): initial notes for postmortem: cause = incompatible prefix hash rollout (v2) with no coordinated warmup; contributing factor = rollout automation allowed 100% completion without observed safety check; mitigation = rollback and selective prefetch; follow-ups = add rollout preflight check for keyspace compatibility, require warmup job to finish before >50% rollout, add automatic cache warmup in rollout pipeline, improve production canary observability for cache-hit deltas.

eva (eng): i'll own action item: add compatibility check and a migration/warmup plan in the release playbook.

alex (eng-releases): i'll add gating rule in the release system: blocked rollout >20% until warmup job reports >=85% hit rate on canary.

ryan (pm): I'll draft external incident note once postmortem is ready. ETA for postmortem doc: EOD tomorrow.

tim (oncall): handing off. @maria you're owner for the postmortem. Closing oncall bridge in 15. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maria (sre): final metrics snapshot (04:49): p95 240ms, p99 490ms, cache_hit_rate 92%, streaming backlog drained. Marking incident resolved in internal tracker.

incident-bot: Incident #INC-4721 resolved. Postmortem link: (to be created)

alex (eng-releases): small follow-up: we'll also add an automated smoke test for the top 100 prefixes to the CI pipeline so future hash changes are verified.

maria (sre): noted. I'll add customer-impact timeline to the PM notes.

ryan (pm): thanks team.

-- end of thread --
